notes: All six full-size PNGs were inspected after rendering.
A first inspection found ambiguous flow and escaped centered text; the renderer was corrected and the set was re-rendered.

The corrected set was inspected in a 640x360-per-frame contact sheet. Primary teaching structure and labels remain legible; dense secondary copy still requires the planned real Echo phone-stage proof.

figures.title: Auction day connects two clocks
figures.caption: The sale connects two legal clocks; it does not end either one instantly.
figures.altText: Two horizontal timelines meet at auction day: arrears, notices and advertisement before it; certificate, possible redemption and deed after it.
figures.teachingJob: Separate the municipality's pre-sale process from the purchaser's post-sale legal route.

figures.title: A parcel sheet is a set of claims to verify
figures.caption: Every field is an identifier or claim to verify, not a promise about the parcel.
figures.altText: Annotated fictional tax-sale packet page pointing to lien number, AAN, PID, recovery amount, assessment, redemption marker, map and legal-description areas.
figures.teachingJob: Explain the common fields in an Inverness-style parcel sheet without reproducing owner data or Property Online material.
figures.rights: Self-created fictional composite; no real parcel, owner or Property Online reproduction.

figures.title: Identifiers help records meet
figures.caption: Identifiers help records meet; none alone proves boundaries, access, condition or value.
figures.altText: Seven labelled record cards form a chain from tax-sale lien to legal description, with unsupported property conclusions separated below.
figures.teachingJob: Keep the lien, AAN, PID, location, assessment, map and legal description in their proper evidentiary roles.
legalLocators: MGA s. 142; Nova Scotia land and assessment record definitions

figures.title: Preserve disagreement between sources
figures.caption: A careful file preserves disagreement instead of silently choosing a convenient number.
figures.altText: Six source cards feed a reconciliation table where a missing detail page, differing recovery amounts and differing auction-result counts remain visibly unresolved.
figures.teachingJob: Show why the summary, detail sheet, live webpage, registry research, result sheet and council record remain separate evidence.
legalLocators: Inverness August 11, 2026 packet; May 27, 2025 packet, results and June 19 council minutes
figures.rights: Self-created diagram from aggregated official counts; no owner or parcel narrative.

figures.title: The ordinary redeemable route
figures.caption: A winning bid may begin a six-month certificate-holder period rather than immediate ownership.
figures.altText: Timeline from full payment to certificate, a six-month certificate-holder period, possible redemption, and a municipal tax deed if redemption does not occur.
figures.teachingJob: Explain the ordinary six-month redemption route while keeping certificate-holder duties visible.
figures.rights: Self-created statutory-process diagram; educational overview only.

figures.title: No redemption period does not mean no uncertainty
figures.caption: Immediate deed changes the redemption route, not possession, access, title quality or buildability.
figures.altText: Short route from older tax arrears to the statutory redemption exception and a requested municipal deed, followed by unresolved branches for possession, access, title review and intended use.
figures.teachingJob: Explain the older-arrears redemption exception without implying instant possession or a problem-free property.
figures.rights: Self-created statutory-process diagram; educational overview only.
